pages.text: The road to Abha twisted up into the mountains like a grey ribbon. Hamad pressed his face against the car window as clouds drifted below them. "We're actually higher than the clouds!" he said. His cousin Yousef laughed, but Uncle Saleh reminded them that mountains could change their mood very quickly.

Early the next morning, the three of them set off along a narrow trail toward a hidden waterfall. Juniper trees grew between the rocks, and baboons watched them from a cliff. Uncle Saleh gave each boy a whistle and a bottle of water. "If you ever get lost, stay calm and blow the whistle three times," he explained.

After two hours, they finally heard the roar of falling water. As Uncle Saleh stepped onto a wet rock to take a photo, his foot slipped. He fell awkwardly and cried out in pain. "I think I've twisted my ankle badly," he said, his face pale.

Yousef checked his phone, but there was no signal at all. Then, without warning, thick fog began to roll down the mountain, hiding the path in white. Hamad felt his heart beating fast. "We can't carry you, Uncle," he said. "What should we do?"

Uncle Saleh thought for a moment. "There's a farm at the bottom of the valley," he said. "Follow the stream downhill and look for the red marks painted on the rocks. Stay together, and don't take any risks."

The boys moved carefully through the fog, which was so dense they could barely see ten metres ahead. Twice they lost the trail, but each time Yousef spotted another faded red mark. When the stream disappeared beneath some huge boulders, Hamad almost panicked. Then he remembered the whistle and blew three long blasts.

From somewhere below, a dog barked, and a man's voice called back. Soon an elderly shepherd appeared out of the mist with his dog beside him. "Assalamu alaikum, boys! What are you doing up here in this weather?" he asked kindly. The boys quickly explained everything.

The shepherd, Abu Nasser, phoned for help from his farm, and two rescuers soon reached Uncle Saleh with a stretcher. That evening, the whole family gathered around Uncle Saleh, whose ankle was wrapped in a bandage. "You two were brave and sensible," he said proudly. Hamad smiled, but he secretly decided that next time he would check the weather forecast first.

grammar.title: Present Perfect Continuous for Recent Habits
grammar.ar: نستخدم المضارع التام المستمر (have/has been + الفعل مع ing) للحديث عن نشاط بدأ في الماضي وما زال مستمرًا حتى الآن، أو عن عادة جديدة في الفترة الأخيرة. غالبًا نضيف كلمات مثل lately و recently و these days. انتبه: لا نقول I am spending a lot of time lately، بل نقول I've been spending a lot of time lately.
examples: I've been spending too much time on games lately.
She's been using a new study app for two weeks.
We've been watching fewer videos since we set a limit.

I'd say the telephone. It was invented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.

grammar.title: Past Passive and Used To
grammar.ar: نستخدم المبني للمجهول في الماضي (was/were + التصريف الثالث للفعل) عندما يكون الاختراع نفسه أهم من الشخص الذي صنعه، ونذكر الفاعل بعد by والسنة بعد in. ونستخدم used to + الفعل في المصدر للحديث عن عادات كانت في الماضي ولم تعد موجودة الآن. انتبه: نقول was invented وليس invented وحدها عندما يكون الاختراع هو الفاعل في الجملة.
examples: The light bulb was invented by Thomas Edison in 1879.
Before cars existed, people used to travel by horse or camel.
The first smartphones were sold in the 1990s.

words.ex: Scientists predict that cars will drive themselves in the future.
AI might help teachers check homework faster.
With virtual reality, we could visit the pyramids without leaving class.
In a smart home, you can control the lights with your voice.
Some people worry about their privacy when devices listen to them.
It's unlikely that robots will replace all teachers.

dialogue.t: What do you think schools will be like in 2040?
By 2040, I think we'll have virtual reality lessons. We could explore space in science class!
That sounds amazing. Do you think robots will replace teachers?
No, it's unlikely that robots will replace teachers completely. Students still need real people.
I agree. What about our homes?
It's likely that most homes will be smart homes. The fridge might order food by itself.
Is there anything that worries you about the future?
I hope AI will make life easier, but I'm worried that we'll lose our privacy.

grammar.title: Making Predictions: will, likely and unlikely
grammar.ar: نستخدم will + الفعل في المصدر للتنبؤ بالمستقبل حسب رأينا، وغالبًا مع I think أو I don't think. وللتعبير عن درجة الاحتمال نقول It's likely that (من المحتمل أن) أو It's unlikely that (من غير المحتمل أن) ثم جملة كاملة. لاحظ أننا نقول عادةً I don't think we'll... بدلًا من I think we won't...
examples: By 2040, I think we'll have flying taxis in big cities.
It's likely that students will use AI tutors at home.
I don't think paper books will disappear completely.

words.ex: The deadline for our science project is next Friday.
Let's divide up the work so nobody has too much to do.
Can you take care of the research while I make the slides?
Maya is in charge of the experiment, so ask her about the results.
If we work hard this week, we'll stay on schedule.
You can rely on me. I'll finish my part on time.

dialogue.t: So, our science project on plant growth is due on the 20th. How should we divide up the tasks?
Well, I'm good at drawing, so I could design the poster.
Great. Why don't you take care of the poster while I write up the experiment results?
Sounds fair. But who's going to measure the plants every day?
We could take turns. You do Mondays and Wednesdays, and I'll do the other days.
OK. Let's make sure we finish all the measurements by next Thursday.
Good idea. And let's make sure we practise the presentation by the 18th, so we have time to fix any problems.
Deal. I'll send us both a reminder so we stay on schedule.

grammar.title: Making suggestions and offers
grammar.ar: نستخدم Why don't you + الفعل في صورته الأساسية (بدون to) لاقتراح مهمة على شخص آخر، و while I لنقول ما سنفعله نحن في الوقت نفسه. ونستخدم Let's make sure we + الفعل + by + وقت لنتفق على موعد نهائي. أما للعرض فنقول I'm good at + اسم أو فعل بـ ing، ثم so I could + الفعل. انتبه: نقول good at وليس good in.
examples: Why don't you take care of the graphs while I check the spelling?
Let's make sure we send the report to the teacher by Sunday evening.
I'm good at speaking in public, so I could present our results.

words.ex: I think you misunderstood me. I wasn't angry with you.
I'm sorry I forgot to call you. I didn't do it on purpose.
Try to see the problem from her point of view.
He was upset because nobody told him about the meeting.
Please don't blame me. It wasn't my fault.
Let's talk calmly and sort out this problem together.

dialogue.t: Hey Layla, are you upset with me? You didn't reply to my messages.
Well, yes. You told the teacher I didn't do my part of the project.
Oh no! I think you might have misunderstood what I said. I told her your part wasn't finished yet, not that you didn't do it.
Really? From my point of view, it sounded like you were blaming me.
I'm really sorry. I didn't mean to make you look bad. I just wanted to explain why we needed more time.
OK, I understand now. And I didn't mean to ignore you. I was just angry.
Let's sort it out. Next time, we can talk to the teacher together.
That's a good idea. Thanks for explaining.

grammar.title: Polite language to fix misunderstandings
grammar.ar: نستخدم I didn't mean to + الفعل الأساسي لنقول إننا لم نقصد فعل شيء سيئ. ونستخدم I think you might have + التصريف الثالث (مثل misunderstood) لنقول بلطف إن الشخص الآخر ربما فهم خطأ، فهي أهدأ من قول You're wrong. وعبارة From my point of view تقدّم رأيك دون هجوم. تذكّر أن mean تصبح meant في الماضي، لكن بعد didn't نستخدم mean.
examples: I didn't mean to take your seat. I didn't know it was yours.
I think you might have misunderstood the instructions.
From my point of view, we both made a mistake.

words.ex: I always feel stressed out the week before exams.
I need to revise maths tonight because the test is tomorrow.
A revision timetable helps me plan what to study each day.
After an hour of studying, I take a break and go for a walk.
I can't concentrate when my phone is next to me.
If you don't get enough sleep, you'll feel tired in the exam.

dialogue.t: You look tired, Yousef. Are you OK?
Not really. I'm so stressed out about the final exams. I can't concentrate on anything.
Have you tried making a revision timetable? It shows you exactly what to study each day.
No, I haven't. I usually just study whatever I find first.
It might help if you took short breaks every hour, too. Your brain needs some rest.
That makes sense. What would you do if you had three exams in two days?
I'd start with the hardest subject, and I'd make sure I got enough sleep before each exam.
Thanks, that's really helpful. I'll try it tonight.

grammar.title: Giving advice and asking for opinions
grammar.ar: بعد Have you tried نستخدم الفعل مع ing، مثل Have you tried reading؟ وليس to read. في عبارة It might help if you نستخدم غالبًا الفعل في الماضي البسيط (took, went) لأننا نتحدث عن موقف متخيَّل، وهي نصيحة لطيفة غير مباشرة. ولسؤال صديق عن رأيه في موقف خيالي نستخدم What would you do if + الماضي البسيط؟ والجواب يكون I'd + الفعل الأساسي.
examples: Have you tried studying with a friend?
It might help if you turned off your phone while you revise.
What would you do if you forgot everything in the exam?

words.ex: Could you pass on the message to Omar? He wasn't here today.
The coach gave us clear instructions before the match.
Our next training session is on Wednesday after school.
We have to hand in our essays by Monday.
Can you remind me to bring my football boots?
Sami was absent yesterday because he was ill.

dialogue.t: Hi Sami, you missed the training session yesterday. The coach asked about you.
I was ill. Did he say anything important?
Yes. He said that the match was moved to Saturday morning.
Saturday? OK. Anything else?
They told us to bring our own water bottles and to arrive at eight o'clock.
Got it. Oh, and did Ms Huda say anything in science class?
She asked me if you had finished your lab report. She said that you could hand it in on Monday.
Great, thanks for passing on the message!

grammar.title: Reported speech: statements, questions and instructions
grammar.ar: عندما ننقل كلام شخص آخر نستخدم said that، وعادةً نرجع زمن الفعل خطوة إلى الماضي: is تصبح was، و can تصبح could، و will تصبح would. ولنقل سؤال جوابه نعم أو لا نستخدم asked (me) if + جملة عادية بدون do/does وبترتيب الخبر، وليس بترتيب السؤال. ولنقل الأوامر نستخدم told + الشخص + to + الفعل. انتبه: told يحتاج دائمًا إلى شخص بعده (told us)، أما said فلا.
examples: He said that the bus would leave at seven.
She asked me if I was coming to the party.
The coach told us to warm up for ten minutes.

words.ex: I'm torn between the art club and the drama club.
Let's write down the pros and cons of each choice.
I need some time to weigh up my options.
Have you made up your mind about the school trip?
Joining the team is a big commitment. You have to train three times a week.
I don't want to give up football, but I don't have enough time.

dialogue.t: You look worried, Karim. What's wrong?
I'm torn between the football team and the coding club. They both meet on Tuesdays.
That's a tough one. Have you thought about the pros and cons?
Yes. On the one hand, I love football and all my friends are on the team. On the other hand, coding could really help me in the future.
Could you do one this term and the other one next term?
Maybe. I've been weighing it up all week, but it's still hard to make up my mind.
So, what did you choose in the end?
In the end, I decided to join the coding club because the football season finishes in March, and I can join the team again next year.

grammar.title: Talking about choices and decisions
grammar.ar: نستخدم I'm torn between X and Y لنقول إننا محتارون بين خيارين، وبعدها اسم أو فعل بـ ing. ونستخدم On the one hand ... On the other hand ... لعرض جانبين مختلفين من الموضوع. ولنقول ما اخترناه في النهاية نستخدم In the end, I decided to + الفعل الأساسي + because + السبب. انتبه: نقول decided to join وليس decided join أو decided for join.
examples: I'm torn between learning Spanish and learning French.
On the one hand, the trip is exciting. On the other hand, it's very expensive.
In the end, I decided to stay at home because I had a lot of homework.

words.ex: I regret not saying sorry to my friend sooner.
Everyone makes mistakes. The important thing is to learn from them.
I learned an important lesson: always check your work.
He always does his homework at the last minute.

words.ar: يتأمّل في الماضي / ينظر إلى الوراء
words.ex: When I look back, I can see that I was too impatient.
If I could start again, I would do things differently.

dialogue.t: Looking back, do you have any regrets from this school year?
Yes, one big one. I left my history project until the last minute, and I got a really bad mark.
Oh no. What happened?
I stayed up all night and made lots of silly mistakes. I wish I had started earlier.
Something similar happened to me with the science fair. If I had known how long it would take, I would have asked for help sooner.
So what lesson did you learn?
Next time, I'll make sure to plan everything on a calendar.
Good idea. Next time, I'll make sure to start on the same day I get the task.

grammar.title: Regrets: wish + past perfect and the third conditional
grammar.ar: للتعبير عن الندم على شيء حدث في الماضي نستخدم I wish I had + التصريف الثالث (مثل I wish I had studied). وللحديث عن ماضٍ لا يمكن تغييره نستخدم الشرط الثالث: If I had + التصريف الثالث، ثم I would have + التصريف الثالث. وللحديث عن خطة في المستقبل بعد تعلّم الدرس نستخدم Next time, I'll make sure to + الفعل الأساسي. انتبه: لا نستخدم would في الجزء الذي يبدأ بـ if.
examples: I wish I had listened to my teacher's advice.
If I had known about the test, I would have revised more.
Next time, I'll make sure to check the deadline.

words.ar: يحافظ على المياه / يرشّد استهلاك المياه
words.ex: We should all conserve water because it is very precious in our region.
Native trees like the ghaf tree need very little water to grow.
Many plants die during a long drought.
Our class made a plan to reduce waste in the school canteen.
The Saudi Green Initiative aims to plant billions of trees across the Kingdom.
Trees give shade and keep our streets cooler in summer.

dialogue.t: Have you read about the Saudi Green Initiative? It aims to plant ten billion trees across the Kingdom.
Yes! I think we ought to help in order to make our neighbourhood greener.
But trees need water, and water is precious here.
True. If everyone turned off the tap while brushing their teeth, we could save thousands of litres every day.
Good point. One thing our school could do is collect the water from the air conditioners and use it for the plants.
That's realistic! We ought to choose native trees in order to save even more water.
Let's suggest both ideas to our head teacher tomorrow.
Great. I'll write the proposal tonight.

grammar.title: Suggestions and purpose: ought to / in order to
grammar.ar: نستخدم ought to مع الفعل في صورته الأساسية لتقديم اقتراح أو نصيحة، ومعناها قريب من should أي «ينبغي». ونستخدم in order to مع الفعل في صورته الأساسية لبيان الهدف، بمعنى «لكي». انتبه: لا نضع to بعد should، أما ought فلا بد أن تتبعها to دائمًا.
examples: We ought to plant more trees in order to reduce the heat in our cities.
Families ought to fix leaking taps in order to save water.
Our school ought to start a recycling club in order to reduce waste.

words.ex: Saudi Arabia will host the FIFA World Cup in 2034.
The new stadium will have seats for more than 40,000 fans.
Big sporting events can help tourism grow very quickly.
The country is improving its infrastructure, such as roads, airports and metro lines.
I'd love to volunteer at a big event and help visitors find their way.
The World Cup is a great opportunity to show our culture to the world.

dialogue.t: Saudi Arabia is hosting the World Cup in 2034! I'm really looking forward to watching a match in a real stadium.
Me too! It will give young players the chance to see world-class football up close.
And millions of fans are expected to visit the country.
That means more hotels and better transport. It will give local businesses the chance to grow.
Do you think it will change ordinary people's lives too?
I think so. More people are expected to start playing sport, and that's good for everyone's health.
By 2034, I'll be in my twenties. Maybe I'll work as a volunteer!
That would be amazing. I'm looking forward to volunteering too.

grammar.title: looking forward to + -ing / be expected to
grammar.ar: بعد عبارة looking forward to نستخدم الفعل مع ing أو اسمًا، لأن to هنا حرف جر وليست جزءًا من الفعل. لذلك نقول I'm looking forward to watching وليس to watch. أما be expected to فيليها الفعل في صورته الأساسية، ومعناها «من المتوقع أن».
examples: I'm really looking forward to meeting fans from all over the world.
The new metro is expected to open before the tournament.
We're looking forward to the opening ceremony.

words.ex: The headline sounded shocking, but the story was boring.

words.ar: على ما يبدو / حسب ما يُقال
words.ex: Apparently, the new park will open next month.
Fake news spreads very fast on social media.
Always check the story with a reliable source before you share it.
There's a rumour that our school trip is cancelled, but nobody knows for sure.
Journalists fact-check every story before they publish it.

dialogue.t: Did you hear that a camel in Riyadh learned to use a lift by itself?
Really? Where did you read that?
Apparently, it was on a website I found yesterday. There's even a video.
Hmm, that can't be true because camels are far too big for a normal lift.
You're right. And the website only had strange stories, no real news.
Then it must be fake. Real news usually appears on more than one reliable source.
OK, what about this one? Did you hear that scientists discovered a new kind of frog last year?
That must be true because scientists find new species every year. But let's fact-check it anyway.

grammar.title: Deduction: must / can't
grammar.ar: نستخدم must مع الفعل في صورته الأساسية عندما نكون متأكدين تقريبًا أن الشيء صحيح بناءً على دليل. ونستخدم can't عندما نكون متأكدين أنه مستحيل أو غير صحيح. انتبه: عكس must في الاستنتاج هو can't وليس mustn't، لأن mustn't تعني «ممنوع».
examples: That story must be real because it's on every news channel.
This photo can't be real because the shadows are wrong.
He must be tired; he has been travelling all day.

words.ex: My older sister is my role model because she works so hard.
I admire people who help others without expecting anything back.
She was determined to finish the race even though she was tired.
He overcame many difficulties to become a doctor.
You can achieve your goals if you never give up.
Even after winning the prize, he stayed humble and kind.

dialogue.t: Who inspires you the most?
Rayyanah Barnawi. She's someone who followed her dream and never gave up.
Isn't she the first Saudi woman to travel to space?
Yes, in 2023. She has achieved so much by studying science for many years and doing research.
That's impressive! What do you admire most about her?
What I admire most is the way she encourages young people to love science. What about you?
My grandfather. He's someone who always helps our neighbours. What I admire most is the way he stays patient with everyone.
He sounds like a great role model.

grammar.title: Describing people: who / by + -ing
grammar.ar: نستخدم who بعد كلمة تدل على شخص مثل someone أو a person لنضيف وصفًا له، ولا نكرر الضمير بعدها، فنقول someone who helps وليس someone who he helps. ونستخدم by مع الفعل المنتهي بـ ing لنشرح الطريقة التي حقق بها الشخص شيئًا، بمعنى «عن طريق».
examples: My teacher is someone who always believes in her students.
He became a champion by training every single day.
She has helped many families by starting a charity in her city.

words.ex: Good communication skills are important in almost every job.
A job outdoors would really suit someone who loves nature.
Many future jobs will involve working with artificial intelligence.
Engineers in renewable energy design solar and wind power projects.
You need to be creative to work as a game designer.
She wants a career in medicine because she loves helping people.

dialogue.t: Have you thought about what you want to do in the future?
I'm thinking of becoming a data scientist because I love maths and computers.
Cool. To do this job, you need to be patient and good at solving problems.
Exactly. What about you?
I'm not sure yet. I'd rather work outdoors than sit in an office all day.
Then maybe you could be a renewable energy engineer. Saudi Arabia is building huge solar farms.
That sounds interesting! But to do this job, you need to be good at physics.
Well, you'd rather study physics than work in an office, right?

grammar.title: Preferences: would rather ... than ...
grammar.ar: نستخدم would rather للتعبير عن تفضيل شيء على آخر، ويأتي بعدها الفعل في صورته الأساسية بدون to. نضع than قبل الخيار الثاني، ويكون الفعل بعدها أيضًا في صورته الأساسية. وفي الكلام نختصر I would إلى I'd.
examples: I'd rather design apps than repair cars.
She'd rather work in a team than work alone.
We'd rather study engineering than business.

words.ex: Start by introducing your topic clearly in one sentence.
My main point is that every student can help the environment.
Some jobs, for example drone pilots, didn't exist twenty years ago.
Look at your audience when you are speaking.
In your conclusion, repeat your most important idea.
At the end, summarise your talk in two or three sentences.

dialogue.t: Today I'd like to talk about how our school can save water.
First of all, we could fix all the leaking taps. One dripping tap can waste a lot of water every day.
Another point is that we could use water from the air conditioners for the school garden.
To sum up, small changes at school can make a big difference for our environment. Thank you for listening.
Thank you, that was very clear. Which idea do you think is the easiest to start with?
I think fixing the taps is the easiest, because it's quick and doesn't cost much.
Good answer. And how could students help?
Students could report leaking taps to the teachers and remind their friends to turn off the water.

grammar.title: Structuring a talk with linking phrases
grammar.ar: لكي يكون عرضك واضحًا، قسّمه إلى بداية ووسط ونهاية. نبدأ بعبارة Today I'd like to talk about لتقديم الموضوع، ثم نرتّب الأفكار بعبارات مثل First of all وAnother point is وFinally. وفي النهاية نستخدم To sum up لتلخيص الفكرة الرئيسية قبل شكر الجمهور.
examples: Today I'd like to talk about the jobs of the future.
First of all, technology is changing very fast. Another point is that new skills are needed.
To sum up, we need to keep learning to be ready for the future.
